### Remove the two measured transfer stalls: per-piece fdatasync and Nagle on peer streams

`completed` · `@templartorrent.milestone.loopback-throughput/1`

AGENTS.md step 5: optimize from evidence. The 32 MiB loopback scenario ran at about 6 MB/s on tmpfs and 1.5 to 2.2 MB/s on a real btrfs disk. Two causes, each measured alone: FileStore synced every 16 KiB piece although the resume checkpoint's sync_all is the only barrier the bitmap needs (DESIGN.md: persist batched changes, sync before marking resume bits durable), and no peer stream set TCP_NODELAY, so each pipelined Request waited for a delayed ACK. Fix both without weakening the resume guarantee and record before/after with attribution.

> **Note:** Fixture seeders share rbit's transport, so they also gained nodelay; a client-only variant was measured separately.

### Bounded parser and engine fuzzing with every found crash fixed and pinned

`completed` · `@templartorrent.milestone.parser-fuzzing/1`

DESIGN.md section 10 requires bounded parser fuzzing. Add libFuzzer targets, in their own workspace outside the shipping graph, for every parser that remote or on-disk bytes reach (tracker HTTP and announce body, metainfo and the BEP-9 info envelope, magnet and tracker URL, peer wire and extension messages, bencode, persisted session records) plus a stateful engine-session target under adversarial peer behaviour. Fix every crash at its source, including in the rbit fork, and pin each with a stable-toolchain regression test that fails before the fix.

### Public-swarm client: verified Ubuntu ISO download from the Internet with UDP trackers, dual-stack, DHT, PEX and MSE

`completed` · `@templartorrent.milestone.public-swarm-client/1`

Close the gaps that kept the client from replacing Deluge or Transmission on public torrents: per-family (BEP 7) HTTP and UDP (BEP 15) announces, a fixed dual-stack listen port, .torrent files added from their own info dictionary instead of BEP-9, non-blocking peer connects, DHT (BEP 5), PEX (BEP 11), MSE/PE encryption with plaintext fallback, an own peer-ID prefix, more than 128 files, and hybrid torrents through the v1 path with BEP 47 pad files. Pure v2 stays refused with a visible reason. The user permitted an opt-in Internet smoke test with ubuntu-26.04.1-desktop-amd64.iso.torrent on 2026-10-25.

> **Note:** Baseline on 2026-10-25: adding the Ubuntu .torrent failed in 3.9 s with 'no permitted peer supplied valid metadata'. Announces went over IPv4 only and the tracker returned 1 peer, against 25 (24 IPv6) over IPv6.

### HTTP(S) file downloads in the same queue, proven on localhost fixtures

`completed` · `@templartorrent.milestone.http-downloads/1` · after `@templartorrent.milestone.reachability/1`

Implement decision http-download-manager: URL jobs in the existing queue and Add dialog (one URL or a bounded batch, the folder browser, pause, resume, retry, cancel, the remove dialog with the data checkbox defaulting to keeping files), on the rustls transport with name checks, a redirect cap and address admission behind --allow-local-urls; ranged parallel parts reserved from the global payload budget and the shared download rate; resume only under a matching ETag or Last-Modified; a 30 s no-data cut per connection; temporary sibling, fsync, rename; em dash for unknown sizes; optional SHA-256 before completion; persistence through the session store with restore on launch. Torrent behaviour keeps working.

### Protected storage, crash/private-discovery tests, capability gates and peer preference

`completed` · `@templartorrent.milestone.safety-and-peer-policy/1` · after `@templartorrent.milestone.native-app-wiring/1`

AGENTS.md step 4 on the Linux production client: protected handle-relative storage and deletion with explicit refusals, resume and forced-crash restart tests, private-discovery scope tests, v2/hybrid capability gates that reject with a visible reason, and offline country/client/peer-preference integration (Prefer/Normal/Avoid/Block applied locally by the Driver and exposed in the Peers tab).

> **Note:** Opened 2026-10-22 after milestones for AGENTS steps 2 and 3 completed. Peer preference is local only: it orders upload slots, narrows or keeps request pipelines, decides retention when caps shrink, and Block closes and refuses the peer's IP for that job. It is not automatic peer scoring.

### Session persistence: jobs, settings and preferences survive a restart

`completed` · `@templartorrent.milestone.session-persistence/1` · after `@templartorrent.milestone.safety-and-peer-policy/1`

DESIGN.md sections 1 and 7: the Linux client saves schema-versioned per-job records (original torrent bytes, destination, running or paused intent, file selection and order, tracker URLs, peer preferences) and global settings under the XDG data directory with atomic temp-file-and-rename writes, and on the next launch restores every job through a disk recheck off the UI thread without contacting any peer or tracker that the job did not already know. Removal deletes the record. A corrupt or oversized record is skipped with a visible reason, never a panic.

> **Note:** Opened 2026-10-22 after the step 4 milestone completed. No resume bitmap is persisted yet: every launch rechecks from disk, which is the conservative choice DESIGN.md permits. Restoring a job does not re-resolve metadata over the network because the torrent bytes are kept.

### Optimize the measured hot spot: O(P) piece selection

`completed` · `@templartorrent.milestone.picker-optimization/1` · after `@templartorrent.milestone.performance-baselines/1`

AGENTS.md step 5, second half, driven by the 2026-10-22 baseline: the reference piece pick scans every piece per call (about 3 us at 1k pieces, 170 to 350 us at 100k, 4.8 ms at 1M on the documented laptop) while the AVX2 eligibility kernel shows no consistent gain over scalar. Replace the per-pick full scan with per-rank availability buckets or dirty candidate windows in the live engine, keep the dependency-free scalar Sequence as the oracle, and prove equal picks against it on randomized fixtures plus repeated before/after microbench and one whole-scenario localhost measurement. Do not integrate the AVX2 kernel into the picker unless the same evidence shows a win.

> **Note:** Proposed 2026-10-22; not started. PERFORMANCE.md optimization acceptance applies: no correctness, privacy or safety regression, repeated whole-scenario improvement, oracle and boundary tests re-run after the change.

### Close the strict native-source audit for the default build

`completed` · `@templartorrent.milestone.native-source-gate/1` · after `@templartorrent.milestone.picker-optimization/1`

Remove ring, rustls and reqwest from the workspace dependency graph by forking rbit 0.2.2 in-tree with reqwest optional, announce to HTTP trackers over an application-owned bounded transport, refuse https trackers with a visible reason, and document the remaining accepted boundary (OS bindings such as libc, wayland-sys, drm-sys, linux-raw-sys and pure-Rust build scripts).

> **Note:** Opened 2026-10-22 after the owner chose the fork option for question ring-release-gate. HTTPS tracker support stays open as a separate, explicitly visible limitation.
